pamphlet_excerpts: Rowing Blisters Likely: In rowing, blisters are most likely to occur on the hands.
Pay Attention Tender: Pay attention to any tender or sensitive areas (hot spots) thatindicate the start of a blister.
Adjust Relaxyour Grip: You may be able to adjust or relaxyour grip to avoid friction on the sensitive area.
Prevent Them Wearing: If you are prone to blisters, prevent them by wearing rowing gloves.
step_by_step_procedure: Cover Protect Area: If you do get a blister, cover and protect the area from further irritation.
Sprain Occurs Ankle: A sprain occurs when an ankle, wrist, or other joint is bent farenough to overstretch the ligaments, the tough bands that holdjoints together.
Strain Occurs Muscles: A strain occurs when muscles are overstretched, creating tears in the muscle fibers.
Minor Sprains Strainscause: Minor sprains and strainscause only mild discomfort, but more serious sprains and strainsmight be temporarily disabling.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Alone or with a passenger, do the following in either a fixed-seat or sliding-seat rowboat: (1) Launch. (2) Row in a straight line for 100 yards. Stop, pivot, and return to the starting point. (3) Backwater in a straight line for 25 yards. Make a turn underway and return to the starting point. (4) Land and moor or rack your craft. (5) Tie the following mooring knots—clove hitch, roundturn with two half-hitches, bowline, Wellman's knot, and mooring hitch. (b) Participate as a rowing team member in a competitive rowing meet. The team may be sponsored by a school, club, or Scout unit. The meet must include competition between two or more teams with different sponsors. Complete at least 10 hours of team practice prior to the meet.

pamphlet_excerpts: Your hands Gunwales Weight: Step in with your hands on the gunwales, keep your weight low and centered, then quickly turn and sit on the midship seat.
Remember Sight Person: Remember to keep sight of the person who needs help andto push the bow of the boat in the direction you want to go.
Forward Momentum Advantage: Use this forward momentum to your advantage while you getin position and prepare to row.
Soon Seated Slipon: As soon as you are seated, slipon the life jacket and put the oars in the out position.
step_by_step_procedure: Lookover Shoulder Fix: Lookover your shoulder to fix your direction toward the person inthe water and begin rowing.
Approach Swimmer Thewind: Always make your approach to a swimmer into thewind or against the current.
Remember Wavesor Rough: Remember also that wavesor rough water can make launching from shoredangerous.
Comparatively Mild Interval: Usually, a comparatively mild interval willfollow a series of heavy waves.
